memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'As for those of you who are left, I will make their hearts so fearful in
the lands of their enemies that the sound of a windblown leaf will put
them to flight. They will run as though fleeing from the sword, and they
will fall, even though no one is pursuing them'" - Lev 26:36-37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a vivid and tragic picture. People so gripped by fear that the sound
of a leaf blown by the wind sends them running. They flee from enemies who
are not even there, falling over one another in panic, though no one
pursues.

This describes the inner torment that follows a life cut off from God. When
the peace of God is gone, fear rushes in to fill the space. And fear, once
it takes hold, distorts everything — turning shadows into swords and
rustling leaves into armies.

Dear reader, many people live exactly like this, even in comfortable
circumstances. They are pursued by fears that are not real — anxieties
about what might happen, dread of imagined threats, a constant unease with
no visible cause. They flee from shadows.

Where does peace come from? Not from the absence of danger, but from the
presence of God. Proverbs says the wicked flee though no one pursues, but
the righteous are as bold as a lion (Prov 28:1). The difference is not
circumstances; it is whose you are.

Paul writes that God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love
and a sound mind (2 Tim 1:7). John says perfect love drives out fear (1
John 4:18). The love of God, poured into a heart, pushes the shadows back.

If you are fleeing from shadows today, the answer is not to fight the
fears one by one. It is to return to the God whose presence is peace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "shadows" am I fleeing from that may not be real?
2. Has fear filled a space where God's peace should be?
3. How can I return to God's presence as the source of my courage?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I confess the fears that chase me, real and imagined. Fill me with
Your perfect love that drives out fear, and let Your presence be my peace.
Amen.
